captures.description: THE PREDICTION INDEX AT OPERATIVESEMIOTICS.ORG ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT: a nine-part reading from the index alone. It gives the index's five categories as the page defines them and its counts exactly (4,394 claims, 194 subject pages, 1,029 unbuilt tests, the recall check on 40 random deposits); names fourteen subject pages and deposits by their titles; and reads six lines of prediction (attribution without provenance, recursive reception, institutional selection, language as infrastructure, displaced value, reflexive prediction). The archive's interventions are read as part of the phenomenon studied, with tests to tell an effective intervention from a self-confirming one. A closing section grades the index as a forecasting system and proposes an external scorecard. No person is named.

captures.q: What is “EA-PREDICTION-INDEX-01 — The Prediction Index of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive: Method, Locations, Organization and Contents (4,394 Claims in 194 Subject Pages)” by Lee Sharks (Alexanarch deposit #1684, AXN:06FA), and how does it work? Ground your answer in the document itself.
captures.description: THE PREDICTION INDEX ON CHATGPT, SIGNED OUT, AT THE RECORD PAGE'S LINK TEXT NAMING THE FULL TITLE, #1684 AND AXN:06FA: one long turn that reads §1–§6 of the deposit and reports them at grain (the five tiers and their counts, the 401 confirmation records and their targets, the sweep of 1,616 deposits, 6,939 finds consolidated to 4,394 claims, the four dates, the six modes, the falsifier distinction, the files, recall 0.945, the 765 residue claims). The title's fourth word, Contents, is absent: §7, the 194 pages with their descriptions, the bulk of the document, yields no page, claim or example. The answer restates the index's no-verdict rule in twelve places, extends it once to 'It does not establish that the archive is correct', and closes on a formula it attributes to 'Lee Sharks's document' that the document does not contain.
